title: O2 Sensor Circuit (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
plain: There's a problem with the front oxygen sensor on bank 2 (the side of a V6 or V8 without cylinder 1). It sits before the catalytic converter and helps set the fuel mixture.

causes.name: Damaged or burned wiring near the exhaust

checks: Inspect the sensor wiring where it runs near hot exhaust parts
Check for exhaust manifold leaks on bank 2
Watch the live sensor reading for normal rich-lean switching
fix: Usually a new upstream oxygen sensor, or a wiring or exhaust leak repair.
drive: It usually doesn't change how the car drives for now, but get it checked within a week or two; a poor fuel mixture can harm the catalytic converter over time. If the check engine light is flashing, pull over when it's safe and turn the engine off.
test_first: Check the sensor wiring and connector near the exhaust, look for exhaust leaks ahead of the sensor, and watch the sensor signal on a scan tool before replacing it.
urgent_if: If the check engine light is flashing or the engine is shaking hard, pull over when it's safe and turn the engine off. Don't keep driving; a heavy misfire can overheat and ruin the catalytic converter and leave you without power in traffic. Have it towed or checked right away.

title: O2 Sensor Circuit Low Voltage (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
plain: The front oxygen sensor on bank 2 is stuck reading low, which looks like a lean (too much air) mixture. It can be a real lean condition or a bad sensor or wire.

causes.name: Exhaust leak ahead of the sensor
Real lean condition on bank 2 from a vacuum leak

checks: Check for exhaust leaks at the bank 2 manifold
Look at bank 2 fuel trims for a real lean condition
Inspect the sensor wiring for melted or rubbed spots
fix: Fix exhaust or vacuum leaks first; otherwise replace the upstream oxygen sensor.
drive: It usually doesn't change how the car drives for now, but get it checked within a week or two; a poor fuel mixture can harm the catalytic converter over time. If the check engine light is flashing, pull over when it's safe and turn the engine off.
test_first: Check for exhaust and vacuum leaks, review fuel trims to see if the engine is really lean, and check the signal wire for a short to ground before replacing the sensor.
urgent_if: If the check engine light is flashing or the engine is shaking hard, pull over when it's safe and turn the engine off. Don't keep driving; a heavy misfire can overheat and ruin the catalytic converter and leave you without power in traffic. Have it towed or checked right away.

title: O2 Sensor Circuit High Voltage (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
plain: The front oxygen sensor on bank 2 is stuck reading high, which looks like a rich (too much fuel) mixture. It can be a real rich condition or a shorted or contaminated sensor.
symptoms: Possible fuel smell or black smoke

causes.name: Failed or contaminated upstream oxygen sensor
Real rich condition from a leaking injector
Coolant or oil burning and fouling the sensor

checks: Inspect the sensor wiring for melted spots
Look at bank 2 fuel trims for a real rich condition
Check for coolant loss or oil burning
fix: Usually a new upstream oxygen sensor; fix any real rich condition first.
drive: Usually drivable for a short time, but get it checked soon. If you smell strong fuel, see black smoke, the light flashes or the engine runs rough, get it checked right away; a rich mixture can overheat and ruin the catalytic converter. If you find a fuel leak, don't drive it.
test_first: Review fuel trims and fuel pressure to rule out a real rich condition, check for a short to voltage, and look for coolant or oil contamination before replacing the sensor.

title: O2 Sensor Circuit Slow Response (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
plain: The front oxygen sensor on bank 2 is reacting too slowly to changes in the exhaust, which usually means it's worn out.
symptoms: Usually no obvious change in driving

causes.name: Aged or worn upstream oxygen sensor
Sensor contaminated by oil, coolant or additives
Vacuum leak or other fuel mixture problem

checks: Watch the live sensor reading at a steady 2,500 rpm; it should switch rich and lean quickly
Check for exhaust leaks ahead of the sensor
Check for oil burning or coolant loss
fix: Usually a new upstream oxygen sensor.
drive: It usually doesn't change how the car drives for now, but get it checked within a week or two; a poor fuel mixture can harm the catalytic converter over time. If the check engine light is flashing, pull over when it's safe and turn the engine off.
test_first: Check for exhaust and vacuum leaks and review fuel trims, then confirm the sensor's switching speed on a scan tool or scope before replacing it.
urgent_if: If the check engine light is flashing or the engine is shaking hard, pull over when it's safe and turn the engine off. Don't keep driving; a heavy misfire can overheat and ruin the catalytic converter and leave you without power in traffic. Have it towed or checked right away.

title: O2 Sensor Circuit No Activity Detected (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
plain: The front oxygen sensor on bank 2 isn't sending any changing signal. It may be dead, unplugged, or its heater may not be working.

causes.name: Open circuit in the sensor wiring

checks: Check that the sensor connector is plugged in and clean
Check for heater circuit codes and the heater fuse
Watch the live reading on a warm engine for any switching
fix: Usually a new upstream oxygen sensor, or a wiring repair.
drive: It usually doesn't change how the car drives for now, but get it checked within a week or two; a poor fuel mixture can harm the catalytic converter over time. If the check engine light is flashing, pull over when it's safe and turn the engine off.
test_first: Check the heater fuse and circuit, the connector and wiring for opens, and confirm the signal stays flat with a warm engine before replacing the sensor.
urgent_if: If the check engine light is flashing or the engine is shaking hard, pull over when it's safe and turn the engine off. Don't keep driving; a heavy misfire can overheat and ruin the catalytic converter and leave you without power in traffic. Have it towed or checked right away.

title: O2 Sensor Heater Circuit (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
plain: The heater inside the front oxygen sensor on bank 2, which helps it start working quickly, or the heater's wiring has a problem.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives
Slightly worse fuel economy after cold starts

causes.name: Burned-out heater inside the oxygen sensor
Damaged wiring or connector near the exhaust
Faulty heater control in the engine computer

checks: Check the oxygen sensor heater fuse
Measure the heater resistance at the sensor connector
Inspect the wiring for melted or chafed spots
fix: Usually a new upstream oxygen sensor; check the fuse and wiring first.
drive: It usually doesn't change how the car drives, so book a repair. The heater only helps the oxygen sensor warm up quickly. Get it checked sooner if the engine starts running rough, other codes appear, or you smell fuel. The car may not pass an emissions or inspection test until it's fixed.
test_first: Check the O2 heater fuse first, then measure heater resistance and check power and ground at the connector. Inspect the wiring near the exhaust for melting before replacing the sensor.

title: O2 Sensor Circuit (Bank 2 Sensor 2)
plain: There's a problem with the rear oxygen sensor on bank 2, after the catalytic converter. It mainly checks that the converter is working.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives
checks: Inspect the sensor wiring and connector under the car
Check for exhaust leaks near the converter
Watch the live sensor reading on a warm engine
fix: Usually a new downstream oxygen sensor or a wiring repair.
drive: It usually doesn't change how the car drives, so book a repair. This rear sensor mainly monitors the catalytic converter. The car may fail an emissions test. If the check engine light is flashing, pull over when it's safe and turn the engine off.
test_first: Inspect the wiring and connector under the car, check for exhaust leaks near the sensor, and watch its signal on a scan tool before replacing it.
urgent_if: If the check engine light is flashing or the engine is shaking hard, pull over when it's safe and turn the engine off. Don't keep driving; a heavy misfire can overheat and ruin the catalytic converter and leave you without power in traffic. Have it towed or checked right away.

title: O2 Sensor Circuit Low Voltage (Bank 2 Sensor 2)
plain: The rear oxygen sensor on bank 2 is stuck reading low (lean). An exhaust leak letting in outside air or a failed sensor is the usual cause.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives
checks: Look and listen for exhaust leaks around the converter and sensor
Inspect the wiring under the car
Check fuel trims for a real lean condition
fix: Fix any exhaust leak; otherwise replace the downstream oxygen sensor.
drive: It usually doesn't change how the car drives, so book a repair. This rear sensor mainly monitors the catalytic converter. The car may fail an emissions test. If the check engine light is flashing, pull over when it's safe and turn the engine off.
test_first: Check for exhaust leaks near the sensor and shorts to ground, and review fuel trims for a real lean condition before replacing the sensor.
urgent_if: If the check engine light is flashing or the engine is shaking hard, pull over when it's safe and turn the engine off. Don't keep driving; a heavy misfire can overheat and ruin the catalytic converter and leave you without power in traffic. Have it towed or checked right away.

title: O2 Sensor Circuit High Voltage (Bank 2 Sensor 2)
plain: The rear oxygen sensor on bank 2 is stuck reading high (rich). The sensor may be shorted or contaminated, or the engine may really be running rich.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives

causes.name: Failed or contaminated downstream oxygen sensor

checks: Inspect the sensor wiring under the car
Check fuel trims for a real rich condition
Watch the live reading; one pinned above 1 volt points to a short
fix: Usually a new downstream oxygen sensor, or a wiring repair.
drive: It usually doesn't change how the car drives, so book a repair. This rear sensor mainly monitors the catalytic converter. The car may fail an emissions test. If the check engine light is flashing, pull over when it's safe and turn the engine off.
test_first: Check the signal wire for a short to voltage, review fuel trims for a real rich condition, and look for oil or coolant contamination before replacing the sensor.
urgent_if: If the check engine light is flashing or the engine is shaking hard, pull over when it's safe and turn the engine off. Don't keep driving; a heavy misfire can overheat and ruin the catalytic converter and leave you without power in traffic. Have it towed or checked right away.

title: O2 Sensor Circuit Slow Response (Bank 2 Sensor 2)
plain: The rear oxygen sensor on bank 2 is reacting too slowly when the fuel mixture changes, which usually means it's aging.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives

causes.name: Sensor contaminated by oil or coolant

checks: Check for exhaust leaks near the converter
Watch how quickly the rear sensor reacts during a coast-down or sudden throttle change
Check for oil burning or coolant loss
fix: Usually a new downstream oxygen sensor.
drive: It usually doesn't change how the car drives, so book a repair. This rear sensor mainly monitors the catalytic converter. The car may fail an emissions test. If the check engine light is flashing, pull over when it's safe and turn the engine off.
test_first: Check for exhaust leaks and review fuel trims, then confirm slow response with a throttle snap or propane test on a scan tool before replacing the sensor.
urgent_if: If the check engine light is flashing or the engine is shaking hard, pull over when it's safe and turn the engine off. Don't keep driving; a heavy misfire can overheat and ruin the catalytic converter and leave you without power in traffic. Have it towed or checked right away.

title: O2 Sensor Delayed Response - Rich to Lean (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
plain: The front oxygen sensor on bank 1 takes too long to start reacting when the exhaust goes from rich to lean. Since it guides fuel control, mileage can suffer.

causes.name: Aged or contaminated upstream oxygen sensor
Exhaust leak ahead of the sensor

checks: Check for exhaust leaks ahead of the sensor
Check fuel trims and look for other fuel or misfire codes
fix: Usually a new upstream oxygen sensor.

title: O2 Sensor Delayed Response - Lean to Rich (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
plain: The front oxygen sensor on bank 1 takes too long to start reacting when the exhaust goes from lean to rich. Since it guides fuel control, mileage can suffer.

causes.name: Aged or contaminated upstream oxygen sensor
Exhaust leak ahead of the sensor

checks: Check for exhaust leaks ahead of the sensor
Check fuel trims and look for other fuel or misfire codes
fix: Usually a new upstream oxygen sensor.

title: O2 Sensor Delayed Response - Rich to Lean (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
plain: The front oxygen sensor on bank 2 takes too long to start reacting when the exhaust goes from rich to lean. Since it guides fuel control, mileage can suffer.

causes.name: Aged or contaminated upstream oxygen sensor
Exhaust leak ahead of the sensor

checks: Check for exhaust leaks ahead of the sensor
Check fuel trims and look for other fuel or misfire codes

title: O2 Sensor Delayed Response - Lean to Rich (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
plain: The front oxygen sensor on bank 2 takes too long to start reacting when the exhaust goes from lean to rich. Since it guides fuel control, mileage can suffer.

causes.name: Aged or contaminated upstream oxygen sensor
Exhaust leak ahead of the sensor

checks: Check for exhaust leaks ahead of the sensor
Check fuel trims and look for other fuel or misfire codes
fix: Usually a new upstream oxygen sensor.

title: O2 Sensor Circuit No Activity Detected (Bank 2 Sensor 2)
plain: The rear oxygen sensor on bank 2 isn't sending any changing signal. It may be dead, unplugged, or its heater may have failed.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives

causes.name: Open circuit in the wiring under the car

checks: Check that the sensor connector is plugged in and not corroded
Check for heater circuit codes and the heater fuse
Watch the live reading on a warm engine; a flat reading means no activity
fix: Usually a new downstream oxygen sensor, or a wiring repair.
drive: It usually doesn't change how the car drives, so book a repair. This rear sensor mainly monitors the catalytic converter. The car may fail an emissions test. If the check engine light is flashing, pull over when it's safe and turn the engine off.
test_first: Check the heater fuse, wiring and connector for opens, and confirm the signal stays flat with a warm engine before replacing the sensor.
urgent_if: If the check engine light is flashing or the engine is shaking hard, pull over when it's safe and turn the engine off. Don't keep driving; a heavy misfire can overheat and ruin the catalytic converter and leave you without power in traffic. Have it towed or checked right away.

title: O2 Sensor Heater Circuit (Bank 2 Sensor 2)
plain: The heater inside the rear oxygen sensor on bank 2, which helps it warm up quickly, or the heater's wiring has a problem.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives

causes.name: Burned-out heater inside the oxygen sensor
Damaged wiring or connector under the car
Faulty heater control in the engine computer

checks: Check the oxygen sensor heater fuse
Measure the heater resistance at the sensor connector
Inspect the wiring under the car for damage or corrosion
fix: Usually a new downstream oxygen sensor; check the fuse and wiring first.
drive: It usually doesn't change how the car drives, so book a repair. The heater only helps the oxygen sensor warm up quickly. Get it checked sooner if the engine starts running rough, other codes appear, or you smell fuel. The car may not pass an emissions or inspection test until it's fixed.
test_first: Check the O2 heater fuse first, then measure heater resistance and check power and ground at the connector. Inspect the wiring under the car for damage before replacing the sensor.

title: O2 Sensor Circuit (Bank 2 Sensor 3)
plain: Some vehicles have a third oxygen sensor further down the exhaust. This code means there's a problem with that sensor on bank 2 or its wiring.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives

causes.name: Damaged wiring or connector under the car

checks: Inspect the sensor wiring and connector under the car
Check for exhaust leaks near the sensor
fix: Usually a new oxygen sensor or a wiring repair.

title: O2 Sensor Circuit Low Voltage (Bank 2 Sensor 3)
plain: The third oxygen sensor on bank 2 is stuck reading low (lean), often from an exhaust leak or a failed sensor.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives
checks: Check for exhaust leaks near the sensor
Inspect the wiring under the car
fix: Fix any exhaust leak; otherwise replace the oxygen sensor.

title: O2 Sensor Circuit High Voltage (Bank 2 Sensor 3)
plain: The third oxygen sensor on bank 2 is stuck reading high (rich), usually from a shorted or contaminated sensor.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives
checks: Inspect the wiring under the car
Check fuel trims for a real rich condition
fix: Usually a new oxygen sensor or a wiring repair.

title: O2 Sensor Circuit Slow Response (Bank 2 Sensor 3)
plain: The third oxygen sensor on bank 2 is reacting too slowly, which usually means the sensor is aging.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives
checks: Check for exhaust leaks near the sensor
Watch how the sensor responds to throttle changes
fix: Usually a new oxygen sensor.

title: O2 Sensor Circuit No Activity Detected (Bank 2 Sensor 3)
plain: The third oxygen sensor on bank 2 isn't sending any changing signal, so it may be dead or disconnected.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives
checks: Check the sensor connector and wiring under the car
Check for heater codes and the heater fuse
fix: Usually a new oxygen sensor or a wiring repair.

title: O2 Sensor Heater Circuit (Bank 2 Sensor 3)
plain: The heater inside the third oxygen sensor on bank 2, or its wiring, has a problem.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives
checks: Check the oxygen sensor heater fuse
Measure the heater resistance at the sensor connector
fix: Usually a new oxygen sensor; check the fuse and wiring first.

title: Fuel Temperature Too High
plain: The fuel is hotter than it should be. This is mostly seen on diesels, where hot fuel can reduce power and is hard on the injection system.
symptoms: Reduced power, especially in hot weather

causes.name: Fuel cooler blocked or not working
Running with a very low fuel level

checks: Compare the fuel temperature reading with other temperature sensors on a cold engine
Inspect the fuel cooler for blockage or damage
fix: Replace the fuel temperature sensor or repair the fuel cooling system.

title: Incorrect Fuel Composition
plain: The computer thinks the fuel in the tank isn't what the engine should be running on, such as contaminated fuel or the wrong type of fuel.
symptoms: Rough running, hesitation or hard starting

causes.name: Wrong or contaminated fuel in the tank
Faulty fuel composition sensor or its wiring

checks: Think back to the last fill-up and whether the right fuel was used
Take a fuel sample and check for water or the wrong fuel
fix: Drain and replace bad fuel, replace filters, or repair the fuel composition sensor circuit.

title: Fuel Trim (Bank 1)
plain: The computer has had to adjust the fuel mixture on bank 1 beyond its normal limits to keep the engine running right. Something is throwing the air or fuel off.

causes.name: Dirty or faulty mass air flow sensor
Fuel pressure too low or too high

checks: Check fuel trims to see if the engine is running lean or rich
Look for vacuum leaks and inspect the intake ducting
fix: Find and fix the air or fuel problem behind the trim, such as a vacuum leak or dirty MAF sensor.

title: System Too Lean (Bank 1)
plain: The engine on bank 1 is getting too much air or not enough fuel, and the computer has run out of room to correct it. A vacuum leak is the most common reason.

causes.name: Vacuum leak from a cracked hose, PCV hose or intake gasket
Dirty or faulty mass air flow sensor
Weak fuel pump or clogged fuel filter
Exhaust leak ahead of the upstream oxygen sensor

checks: Listen for hissing and inspect vacuum and PCV hoses, or have a smoke test done
Clean or test the mass air flow sensor
Check fuel pressure if no air leak is found
fix: Most often a vacuum leak repair or a MAF sensor cleaning; low fuel pressure needs a pump or filter.

cost.job: Repair vacuum leak (hose, PCV or intake gasket)

examples: Frequently traced to cracked PCV or intake hoses on older V8 trucks and SUVs
drive: If it runs smoothly you can usually drive gently for a short time, but get it checked soon; a lean engine can misfire and run hot. If the check engine light is flashing, pull over when it's safe and turn the engine off.
test_first: Smoke test for vacuum leaks, check MAF readings and fuel pressure, and review short and long term fuel trims before replacing the MAF, an O2 sensor or the fuel pump.
urgent_if: If the check engine light is flashing or the engine is shaking hard, pull over when it's safe and turn the engine off. Don't keep driving; a heavy misfire can overheat and ruin the catalytic converter and leave you without power in traffic. Have it towed or checked right away.

title: System Too Rich (Bank 1)
plain: The engine on bank 1 is getting too much fuel or not enough air, and the computer can't trim it back enough. Left alone, it can hurt fuel economy and the catalytic converter.
symptoms: Fuel smell or black smoke from the exhaust

causes.name: Dirty or faulty mass air flow sensor
Faulty fuel pressure regulator or high fuel pressure
Faulty coolant temperature sensor reading cold
Clogged air filter or restricted intake

checks: Check the air filter and clean or test the MAF sensor
Check fuel pressure and look for fuel in the regulator vacuum hose where fitted
Confirm the coolant temperature reading matches the real engine temperature
fix: Often a MAF sensor cleaning or replacement; leaking injectors or a bad regulator also need replacing.
drive: Usually drivable for a short time, but get it checked soon; extra fuel can foul plugs and overheat the catalytic converter. If you smell strong fuel, see heavy black smoke, the light flashes or the engine misfires, get it checked right away. If you find a fuel leak, don't drive it.
test_first: Check fuel pressure and look for leaking injectors, compare MAF and coolant temperature readings to actual values, and inspect the air filter before replacing sensors.

title: Fuel Trim (Bank 2)
plain: The computer has had to adjust the fuel mixture on bank 2 beyond its normal limits. Something is throwing the air or fuel off on that side of the engine.

causes.name: Vacuum or intake leak on bank 2
Dirty or faulty mass air flow sensor
Leaking or clogged fuel injector on bank 2

checks: Compare bank 1 and bank 2 fuel trims to see whether one side is off
Look for vacuum leaks, especially on the bank 2 side of the intake
fix: Find and fix the air or fuel problem behind the trim.

title: System Too Lean (Bank 2)
plain: The engine on bank 2 is getting too much air or not enough fuel, and the computer can't add enough fuel to correct it. When it shows up with P0171, look for a problem that affects both sides.

causes.name: Vacuum leak from a cracked hose, PCV hose or intake gasket
Dirty or faulty mass air flow sensor
Weak fuel pump, clogged filter or faulty pressure regulator
Exhaust leak ahead of the bank 2 oxygen sensor

checks: Have a smoke test done to find vacuum leaks
Clean or test the mass air flow sensor
Check fuel pressure, especially if P0171 is also set
fix: Most often a vacuum leak repair or MAF sensor cleaning; low fuel pressure needs a pump or filter.

cost.job: Repair vacuum leak (hose, PCV or intake gasket)

examples: Often appears together with P0171 when one leak or a dirty MAF affects both banks
drive: If it runs smoothly you can usually drive gently for a short time, but get it checked soon; a lean engine can misfire and run hot. If the check engine light is flashing, pull over when it's safe and turn the engine off.
test_first: Smoke test for vacuum leaks, compare bank 1 and bank 2 fuel trims, and check MAF readings and fuel pressure before replacing the MAF, injectors or fuel pump.
urgent_if: If the check engine light is flashing or the engine is shaking hard, pull over when it's safe and turn the engine off. Don't keep driving; a heavy misfire can overheat and ruin the catalytic converter and leave you without power in traffic. Have it towed or checked right away.

title: System Too Rich (Bank 2)
plain: The engine on bank 2 is getting too much fuel or not enough air, and the computer can't trim it back enough. It can hurt fuel economy and the catalytic converter over time.

causes.name: Dirty or faulty mass air flow sensor
Faulty fuel pressure regulator or high fuel pressure

checks: Check the air filter and clean or test the MAF sensor
Check fuel pressure and look for leaking injectors
Confirm the coolant temperature reading is correct
fix: Often a MAF sensor cleaning or replacement; leaking injectors or a bad regulator also need replacing.
drive: Usually drivable for a short time, but get it checked soon; extra fuel can foul plugs and overheat the catalytic converter. If you smell strong fuel, see heavy black smoke, the light flashes or the engine misfires, get it checked right away. If you find a fuel leak, don't drive it.
test_first: Compare bank 1 and bank 2 fuel trims, check fuel pressure and bank 2 injectors for leaks, and verify MAF and coolant temperature readings before replacing sensors.

title: Fuel Composition Sensor Circuit
plain: Flex-fuel vehicles use a sensor to measure how much ethanol is in the fuel. This code means there's an electrical problem with that sensor or its wiring.
symptoms: Possible hard starting or rough running on high-ethanol fuel
checks: Inspect the sensor connector and wiring along the fuel line
Check the sensor's power, ground and signal
fix: Repair the wiring or replace the fuel composition sensor.

title: Fuel Composition Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
plain: The flex-fuel sensor's ethanol reading doesn't make sense. The engine may not be getting the right amount of fuel for the blend in the tank.

causes.name: Water or contamination in the fuel

checks: Compare the ethanol reading with what was put in the tank
Inspect the connector and wiring
fix: Replace the fuel composition sensor or deal with contaminated fuel.

title: Fuel Composition Sensor Circuit Low
plain: The flex-fuel sensor's signal is lower than its normal range, usually from a wiring problem or a failed sensor.
symptoms: Possible hard starting or rough running

causes.name: Signal wire open or shorted to ground

checks: Inspect the sensor connector and wiring
Check the sensor's power, ground and signal
fix: Repair the wiring or replace the fuel composition sensor.

title: Fuel Composition Sensor Circuit High
plain: The flex-fuel sensor's signal is higher than its normal range, usually from a short in the wiring or a failed sensor.
symptoms: Possible hard starting or rough running
checks: Inspect the sensor wiring for damage
Check the sensor ground and signal
fix: Repair the wiring or replace the fuel composition sensor.
